refutes: U1: observable outputs are identical under every admissible schedule, for any application whose callbacks are deterministic

system.node: fusion-like node with one field of shared state, last_imu, initially 0
system.inputs: one IMU sample v=7 and one scan r=100, both ready at the same instant (the same LF tag, or the same executor wait-set pass)
system.deterministic: each callback is a pure function of its input and last_imu

confluent_control.note: the shared write commutes but the observation does not: on_scan publishes 107 after on_imu and 100 before it, so commuting state updates alone are not confluence

commuting_control.note: no shared state: the multiset of outputs is the same under both orders, the sequence is not

conclusion: Two deterministic callbacks that share state and have two permitted orders give different outputs. Schedule invariance therefore needs an order constraint (one schedule left) or a proof that the remaining choices are confluent for the stated output relation. Neither is derived from repeated runs.
boundary: A model-level fixture, not a ROS 2 run. It makes no statement about which order a given ROS 2 executor picks, and it is not a property of sentry_pipeline, whose fusion_node callbacks keep no state.
